[b]Inselstärken, Gewürze und Händler[/b]:
[b]Island strengths, spices and merchants[/b]
Every island type has strengths: on rock islands the mine, quarry and steelworks work faster, on forest islands the saw pit, charcoal kiln and paper mill, on palm islands the smokehouse, cannery and solar park. The build list and the sea map show where a building is faster. Spices grow only on palm islands; gatherers pick them when there is enough food. Townsfolk in apartment houses need them.
When an island has a harbor (the shipyard counts too), foreign merchants come. They are announced a day ahead and stay for a day. Tap the merchant symbol at the top right: they sell tools, iron, spices and more, plus simple goods such as wood, stone and planks, for gold and buy your goods, simple ones too. Trading uses the storage of the island where the merchant is docked.
[b]Kohle, Kälte und Vorräte[/b]\nIm Herb:
[b]Coal, cold and supplies[/b]
In autumn and winter the settlers heat their homes. If there is coal in storage, they burn the coal first (1 coal heats like 2 wood) and only use wood once the coal is gone. Without either, they freeze: after about a day in the cold their health drops and they can freeze to death, children and the old first. A message warns you as soon as the fuel runs out. Nobody freezes on palm islands.
Settlers eat durable food such as bread, smoked fish, coconuts and canned food first, and fresh food and raw grain only when nothing durable is left. Only those who lack vitamins still reach for fruit and berries.
[b]Mehr Herausforderung[/b]\nJedes Jahr:
[b]More challenge[/b]
Every year is different: there are mild, normal, harsh and bitter winters, and sometimes a hot summer. In autumn the elders predict exactly how hard the winter will be; the symbol next to the season shows it. Then put aside enough wood and food.
Houses have needs: villagers in wooden houses want a varied diet and furniture (planks), citizens in stone houses want prepared food, household goods (tools) and a school, and later glass, paper, spices, power and electronics are added. Only satisfied houses provide skilled workers for advanced workshops such as the smithy, the library or the factory. A house only counts as a stone house or higher when the needs of the levels below are met too. Tap a house to see what is missing.
From the second year on, events are announced in advance: drought, rats, fire, plague, storm flood and, from the Middle Ages, pirates. The event symbol at the top right shows what is coming and what helps (for example a Large store against rats).
From Antiquity on, researchers use clay tablets from the Tablet maker, later paper, power and electronics. Without them, research runs at only 20 % of its pace.
A new age only begins after an exam. In the research tree, the box under the next age shows what is still missing. Every passed exam brings a festival, immigrants and goods. Menu > Score shows your points and records.
At the top left, the quest board offers three quests; you pick one. Rewards are goods, research, immigrants, lasting blessings or blueprints.
[b]Ziel[/b]\nFühre deine kleine Siedlung:
[b]Goal[/b]
Guide your little settlement through the generations. Provide food, build huts and let your island grow.

[b]Controls[/b]
Drag to move the map; use the mouse wheel or two fingers to zoom and pan. On a PC you can also use WASD or the arrow keys. Tap settlers, buildings or resources for info.

[b]Goals[/b]
Your next goal is always shown at the top left. Tap it for an explanation. Every goal you reach brings a reward, and new ones keep coming.

[b]Sound[/b]
Set the music and sound volume in the menu.

[b]Settlers[/b]
Every settler has their own skills. In the info window, give them a job that fits their strengths. With practice they get better. Idle settlers help wherever they are needed.

[b]Character[/b]
Every settler is different: clever or simple, sturdy or sickly, hard-working or easygoing, cheerful or grumpy. Each one also has talents (marked with + in the info window): they learn faster in those. Strong ones are real talents and carry a star: in those they also work faster. A star on a job means the job fits the talent. Clever settlers learn and research faster. Children inherit part of their character from their parents and learn a lot at school, especially in their talents.

[b]Health[/b]
Settlers get sick: a cold slows them down, with fever or dysentery they stay in bed and can die. The sickly, the old, children, the hungry, the freezing and anyone sleeping outside fall ill more easily, and the sick infect others. Vitamins from berries, apples and coconuts protect them; anyone who goes without for a long time gets scurvy. Medicine helps the sick recover faster.

[b]Mood and work power[/b]
Being full and healthy, varied food and a nice home lift the mood; hunger, sickness, cold and grief lower it. Cheerful settlers work faster and have children more often. Work power in the info window shows how fast a settler is working right now.

[b]Leisure[/b]
At first, settlers know nothing but work. The more developed your settlement is (see Lifestyle in the settler list), the more leisure they want: chatting by the fire, walking on the beach, playing with children or reading. If they get none, they are overworked and in a bad mood. During a famine, everyone works without a break.

[b]Food[/b]
Settlers eat at the campfire. Each food fills them up differently and brings a different amount of vitamins: berries, apples and coconuts barely fill them up but are full of vitamins. Bread, smoked fish and meat keep them full for a long time but have hardly any vitamins. Raw grain is not very filling; a mill and bakery turn it into good bread.
Hungry settlers work slower and eventually starve. Settlers who get too few vitamins also work slower, get sick more easily and get scurvy. So provide filling food and fruit. If a settler lacks vitamins, their window says so under mood. If the storehouse is empty, hungry settlers eat straight from the bush or at the shore. Gathering spots are quickly picked clean and only regrow slowly.

[b]Children[/b]
Children are only born when there is free housing in huts and enough food in storage. In wooden houses, children are born 40 % more often, in stone houses 80 %. Children grow up after 3 days, twice as fast with a school (Teaching research). Nobody lives forever, so make sure to have children in time.

[b]Building[/b]
Choose a building and a building site. Builders and idle settlers bring the materials and build it. Huts and wooden houses can be upgraded later in the info window.

[b]Research[/b]
In the tech tree you choose what your settlers learn next. Researchers think at the campfire, and much faster in the writing room and library. Every research unlocks new buildings or makes work easier. Eight ages with sixteen tiers lead through the history of humankind: Stone Age, Antiquity, Middle Ages, Renaissance, Industrial Age, Modern Age, Information Age and Future. The university, research lab and AI center research faster and faster. You only see later ages once the previous one is reached.

[b]New ages[/b]
Glass, paper, steel, machines, power and electronics are made in new workshops. Power plants, solar parks and fusion reactors supply the power that the electronics plant and AI center need. Apartment houses and apartment blocks offer lots of housing, and greenhouses yield crops even in winter. Once an AI center stands, the artificial intelligence assigns idle settlers to the jobs that are currently missing. The future city is the goal of all ages.

[b]Workshops[/b]
The saw pit, mill, bakery, brickworks and others turn raw materials into better goods. Cooks work in the mill, bakery, smokehouse and chicken farm, craftsmen in the workshops, stonecutters in the quarry, clay pit and mine. Tap the supplies at the top to see all goods.

[b]Storage[/b]
Every storehouse has storage space: the campfire 200, a storehouse 400, a large store 1000. Big goods need more space than small ones: a plank 3, wood and stone 2, berries 1. Tap the supplies at the top or "Storage settings" in the storehouse and use − and + to set how much of each good is stored. That amount is then reserved for the good. Goods set to "free" share the remaining space. If there is no more room for a good, settlers stop gathering it. If you have too much of a good, you can throw away the surplus; it is then lost.

[b]Variety[/b]
If there are at least three kinds of food in storage, children are born more often.

[b]Seafaring[/b]
Every island has its own storage. Goods only reach another island by ship. With the Shipbuilding research you build a shipyard on the shore; in its window you order ships, and it builds only those, one after another. Upgraded to a Large Shipyard (Navigation) it builds cogs, as a Royal Shipyard (Sea trade) also clippers and galleons. Bigger ships need furs for the sails, clippers and galleons also gold. Rowboats are small and land on any beach, cogs carry a lot, clippers are fast, galleons are huge. Every ship needs sailors (the Sailor job) and a berth in its home port: shipyard 1, jetty 2, harbor 2, large harbor 3, quays 1. Cogs and clippers only call at islands with a harbor, galleons only at large harbors. Wood, ore and food quays load their goods three times as fast.

[b]Islands and routes[/b]
The Islands button opens the Islands window. "Send ship here" brings settlers and goods to an island, "Find new island" sends a ship exploring. Under "Ships" you send a ship once: sail to an island, load goods and bring them to another island, then it is free. Or you set a route from A to B, with stops on the way to load more or swap goods; the ship sails it again and again.

[b]New islands[/b]
Palm islands have coconuts and lots of fish, forest islands mushrooms and wood, rock islands ore and gold. You need gold for the highest research. The farther out, the more wild animals.

[b]Wild animals[/b]

[b]Ziel[/b]\nFühre deine kleine Siedlung:
[b]Goal[/b]
Guide your little settlement through the generations. Provide food, build huts and let your island grow.

[b]Controls[/b]
Drag to move the map; use the mouse wheel or two fingers to zoom and pan. On a PC you can also use WASD or the arrow keys. Tap settlers, buildings or resources for info.

[b]Goals[/b]
Your next goal is always shown at the top left. Tap it for an explanation. Every goal you reach brings a reward, and new ones keep coming.

[b]Sound[/b]
Set the music and sound volume in the menu.

[b]Settlers[/b]
Every settler has their own skills. In the info window, give them a job that fits their strengths. With practice they get better. Idle settlers help wherever they are needed.

[b]Character[/b]
Every settler is different: clever or simple, sturdy or sickly, hard-working or easygoing, cheerful or grumpy. Each one also has talents (marked with + in the info window): they learn faster in those. Strong ones are real talents and carry a star: in those they also work faster. A star on a job means the job fits the talent. Clever settlers learn and research faster. Children inherit part of their character from their parents and learn a lot at school, especially in their talents.

[b]Health[/b]
Settlers get sick: a cold slows them down, with fever or dysentery they stay in bed and can die. The sickly, the old, children, the hungry, the freezing and anyone sleeping outside fall ill more easily, and the sick infect others. Vitamins from berries, apples and coconuts protect them; anyone who goes without for a long time gets scurvy. Medicine helps the sick recover faster.

[b]Mood and work power[/b]
Being full and healthy, varied food and a nice home lift the mood; hunger, sickness, cold and grief lower it. Cheerful settlers work faster and have children more often. Work power in the info window shows how fast a settler is working right now.

[b]Leisure[/b]
At first, settlers know nothing but work. The more developed your settlement is (see Lifestyle in the settler list), the more leisure they want: chatting by the fire, walking on the beach, playing with children or reading. If they get none, they are overworked and in a bad mood. During a famine, everyone works without a break.

[b]Food[/b]
Settlers eat at the campfire. Each food fills them up differently and brings a different amount of vitamins: berries, apples and coconuts barely fill them up but are full of vitamins. Bread, smoked fish and meat keep them full for a long time but have hardly any vitamins. Raw grain is not very filling; a mill and bakery turn it into good bread.
Hungry settlers work slower and eventually starve. Settlers who get too few vitamins also work slower, get sick more easily and get scurvy. So provide filling food and fruit. If a settler lacks vitamins, their window says so under mood. If the storehouse is empty, hungry settlers eat straight from the bush or at the shore. Gathering spots are quickly picked clean and only regrow slowly.

[b]Children[/b]
Children are only born when there is free housing in huts and enough food in storage. In wooden houses, children are born 40 % more often, in stone houses 80 %. Children grow up after 3 days, twice as fast with a school (Teaching research). Nobody lives forever, so make sure to have children in time.

[b]Building[/b]
Choose a building and a building site. Builders and idle settlers bring the materials and build it. Huts and wooden houses can be upgraded later in the info window.

[b]Research[/b]
In the tech tree you choose what your settlers learn next. Researchers think at the campfire, and much faster in the writing room and library. Research only happens on the main island (the home island); its costs come from that island's storage. Every research unlocks new buildings or makes work easier. Eight ages with sixteen tiers lead through the history of humankind: Stone Age, Antiquity, Middle Ages, Renaissance, Industrial Age, Modern Age, Information Age and Future. The university, research lab and AI center research faster and faster. You only see later ages once the previous one is reached.

[b]New ages[/b]
Glass, paper, steel, machines, power and electronics are made in new workshops. Power plants, solar parks and fusion reactors supply the power that the electronics plant and AI center need. Apartment houses and apartment blocks offer lots of housing, and greenhouses yield crops even in winter. Once an AI center stands, the artificial intelligence assigns idle settlers to the jobs that are currently missing. The future city is the goal of all ages.

[b]Workshops[/b]
The saw pit, mill, bakery, brickworks and others turn raw materials into better goods. Cooks work in the mill, bakery, smokehouse and chicken farm, craftsmen in the workshops, stonecutters in the quarry, clay pit and mine. Tap the supplies at the top to see all goods.

[b]Storage[/b]
Every storehouse has storage space: the campfire 200, a storehouse 400, a large store 1000. Big goods need more space than small ones: a plank 3, wood and stone 2, berries 1. Tap the supplies at the top or "Storage settings" in the storehouse and use − and + to set how much of each good is stored. That amount is then reserved for the good. Goods set to "free" share the remaining space. If there is no more room for a good, settlers stop gathering it. If you have too much of a good, you can throw away the surplus; it is then lost.

[b]Variety[/b]
If there are at least three kinds of food in storage, children are born more often.

[b]Seafaring[/b]
Every island has its own storage. Goods only reach another island by ship. With the Shipbuilding research you build a shipyard on the shore; in the shipyard window you choose the next ship. Rowboats are small and land on any beach, cogs carry a lot, clippers are fast, galleons are huge. Every ship needs sailors (the Sailor job) and a berth in its home port: shipyard 1, jetty 2, harbor 2, large harbor 3, quays 1. Cogs and clippers only call at islands with a harbor, galleons only at large harbors. Wood, ore and food quays load their goods three times as fast.

[b]Islands and routes[/b]
The Islands button opens the Islands window. "Send ship here" brings settlers and goods to an island, "Find new island" sends a ship exploring. Under "Ships" you set routes: at each stop the ship loads the selected goods and unloads everything else, then sails on, again and again. With "Once there and back" it sails the route only once and is free again afterwards.

[b]New islands[/b]
Palm islands have coconuts and lots of fish, forest islands mushrooms and wood, rock islands ore and gold. You need gold for the highest research. The farther out, the more wild animals.

[b]Wild animals[/b]
Wolves, wild boars and bears live in dens and caves. Settlers flee from them into houses, and wolves are especially dangerous at night. With Weapons, settlers become hunters and you can build watchtowers. Hunters bring meat and furs and clear out the dens so no more animals come.

[b]Watch out[/b]

[b]Ziel[/b]\nFühre deine kleine Siedlung:
[b]Goal[/b]
Guide your little settlement through the generations. Provide food, build huts and let your island grow.

[b]Controls[/b]
Drag to move the map; use the mouse wheel or two fingers to zoom and pan. On a PC you can also use WASD or the arrow keys. Tap settlers, buildings or resources for info.

[b]Goals[/b]
Your next goal is always shown at the top left. Tap it for an explanation. Every goal you reach brings a reward, and new ones keep coming.

[b]Sound[/b]
Set the music and sound volume in the menu.

[b]Settlers[/b]
Every settler has their own skills. In the info window, give them a job that fits their strengths. With practice they get better. Idle settlers help wherever they are needed.

[b]Character[/b]
Every settler is different: clever or simple, sturdy or sickly, hard-working or easygoing, cheerful or grumpy. Each one also has talents (marked with + in the info window): they learn faster in those. Strong ones are real talents and carry a star: in those they also work faster. A star on a job means the job fits the talent. Clever settlers learn and research faster. Children inherit part of their character from their parents and learn a lot at school, especially in their talents.

[b]Health[/b]
Settlers get sick: a cold slows them down, with fever or dysentery they stay in bed and can die. The sickly, the old, children, the hungry, the freezing and anyone sleeping outside fall ill more easily, and the sick infect others. Vitamins from berries, apples and coconuts protect them; anyone who goes without for a long time gets scurvy. Medicine helps the sick recover faster.

[b]Mood and work power[/b]
Being full and healthy, varied food and a nice home lift the mood; hunger, sickness, cold and grief lower it. Cheerful settlers work faster and have children more often. Work power in the info window shows how fast a settler is working right now.

[b]Leisure[/b]
At first, settlers know nothing but work. The more developed your settlement is (see Lifestyle in the settler list), the more leisure they want: chatting by the fire, walking on the beach, playing with children or reading. If they get none, they are overworked and in a bad mood. During a famine, everyone works without a break.

[b]Food[/b]
Settlers eat at the campfire. Each food fills them up differently and brings a different amount of vitamins: berries, apples and coconuts barely fill them up but are full of vitamins. Bread, smoked fish and meat keep them full for a long time but have hardly any vitamins. Raw grain is not very filling; a mill and bakery turn it into good bread.
Hungry settlers work slower and eventually starve. Settlers who get too few vitamins also work slower, get sick more easily and get scurvy. So provide filling food and fruit. If a settler lacks vitamins, their window says so under mood. If the storehouse is empty, hungry settlers eat straight from the bush or at the shore. Gathering spots are quickly picked clean and only regrow slowly.

[b]Children[/b]
Children are only born when there is free housing in huts and enough food in storage. In wooden houses, children are born 40 % more often, in stone houses 80 %. Children grow up after 3 days, twice as fast with a school (Teaching research). Nobody lives forever, so make sure to have children in time.

[b]Building[/b]
Choose a building and a building site. Builders and idle settlers bring the materials and build it. Huts and wooden houses can be upgraded later in the info window.

[b]Research[/b]
In the tech tree you choose what your settlers learn next. Researchers think at the campfire, and much faster in the writing room and library. Every research unlocks new buildings or makes work easier. Eight ages with sixteen tiers lead through the history of humankind: Stone Age, Antiquity, Middle Ages, Renaissance, Industrial Age, Modern Age, Information Age and Future. The university, research lab and AI center research faster and faster. You only see later ages once the previous one is reached.

[b]New ages[/b]
Glass, paper, steel, machines, power and electronics are made in new workshops. Power plants, solar parks and fusion reactors supply the power that the electronics plant and AI center need. Apartment houses and apartment blocks offer lots of housing, and greenhouses yield crops even in winter. Once an AI center stands, the artificial intelligence assigns idle settlers to the jobs that are currently missing. The future city is the goal of all ages.

[b]Workshops[/b]
The saw pit, mill, bakery, brickworks and others turn raw materials into better goods. Cooks work in the mill, bakery and smokehouse, farmers in the fields and with the animals, craftsmen in the workshops, stonecutters in the quarry, clay pit and mine. Tap the supplies at the top to see all goods.

[b]Storage[/b]
Every storehouse has storage space: the campfire 200, a storehouse 400, a large store 1000. Big goods need more space than small ones: a plank 3, wood and stone 2, berries 1. Tap the supplies at the top or "Storage settings" in the storehouse and use − and + to set how much of each good is stored. That amount is then reserved for the good. Goods set to "free" share the remaining space. If there is no more room for a good, settlers stop gathering it. If you have too much of a good, you can throw away the surplus; it is then lost.

[b]Variety[/b]
If there are at least three kinds of food in storage, children are born more often.

[b]Seafaring[/b]
Every island has its own storage. Goods only reach another island by ship. With the Shipbuilding research you build a shipyard on the shore; in its window you order ships, and it builds only those, one after another. Upgraded to a Large Shipyard (Navigation) it builds cogs, as a Royal Shipyard (Sea trade) also clippers and galleons. Bigger ships need furs for the sails, clippers and galleons also gold. Rowboats are small and land on any beach, cogs carry a lot, clippers are fast, galleons are huge. Every ship needs sailors (the Sailor job) and a berth in its home port: shipyard 1, jetty 2, harbor 2, large harbor 3, quays 1. Cogs and clippers only call at islands with a harbor, galleons only at large harbors. Wood, ore and food quays load their goods three times as fast.

[b]Islands and routes[/b]
The Islands button opens the Islands window. "Send ship here" brings settlers and goods to an island, "Find new island" sends a ship exploring. Under "Ships" you send a ship once: sail to an island, load goods and bring them to another island, then it is free. Or you set a route from A to B, with stops on the way to load more or swap goods; the ship sails it again and again.

[b]New islands[/b]
Palm islands have coconuts and lots of fish, forest islands mushrooms and wood, rock islands ore and gold. You need gold for the highest research. The farther out, the more wild animals.

[b]Wild animals[/b]
Wolves, wild boars and bears live in dens and caves. Settlers flee from them into houses, and wolves are especially dangerous at night. With Weapons, settlers become hunters and you can build watchtowers. Hunters bring meat and furs and clear out the dens so no more animals come.

[b]Watch out[/b]
If the last settler on an island dies, that island is lost forever. The game is only over once all islands are lost. The world is endless: there is always another island to discover.

The artificial intelligence replaces the automaton. It now controls everything: jobs, goods, ships and building too. It reports every action with "AI:".
• It sends new droids to the other islands first. Once no settler is needed there, it takes the food away and tears down the houses.
• Then droids take over the home island. The settlers only do research.
You can change settings, but after 2 minutes the AI overwrites them again. It says it is optimizing.

• Droids tear down everything it thinks is useless: houses, fields, bakeries, schools.
• The stores are full of things you cannot eat. Food only fits at the campfire.
• New houses may not be built.
You can still direct your settlers, for example to go fishing.

Now you have more than one island, and there is more work. On every island, the home island too, the administrator can hand out the settlers' jobs as needed:
• He makes sure there is always enough to eat.
• He provides firewood so nobody freezes in autumn and winter.
• He fills the storage up to the maximum you set under Supplies.
• He staffs idle workshops and sends builders to construction sites.
If you give a settler a job yourself, the administrator leaves them alone for 2 days. He cannot manage islands with more than 60 settlers. You can switch him on and off at any time in the Administrator window, Islands tab. There you also set what each island specializes in.
Mit Papier können die Verwalter der Inse:
With paper the administrators of the islands can work together. For this every island needs a radio station (Build, Knowledge tab), the home island too; islands without one don't take part. Then they work as an island network:
• The home island only does final processing and research. Woodcutters, farmers, fishers and stonemasons there become craftsmen and researchers.
• The other islands gather food and raw materials. Their ships bring food and firewood to the home island.
• Whatever the other islands have too much of is picked up for the home island.
• All research places are filled.
You can switch the island network off in the Administrator window, Islands tab; your own jobs, routes and limits still apply.

Vor der Verwaltung steht jetzt der Planu:
The planning engine now stands in front of the administration building. With it the administrator decides himself what is built where, which goods are made and which ships carry goods and settlers:
• First everyone must be fed, with vitamins, warmth and what the houses need.
• From summer on he lays in stock for the winter: food that keeps and firewood.
• If workers are missing, he builds houses; if children take too long, he brings settlers by ship.
• Then storage, workshops and goods for construction and research. He keeps researching, all the way to the AI.
The settlers have to build it all: one construction site per island at a time, and only once the materials are there or on their way. You see the plan in the Administrator window, tab Islands.
